claim: Auto-regressive LLMs cannot, by themselves, do planning or self-verification; the LLM-Modulo Framework instead pairs LLMs (as approximate knowledge sources generating candidates) with external model-based verifiers in tight bi-directional interaction.
stance_target: intrinsic self-correction fails without external verification, as a settled theoretical position in the 2024 LLM reasoning/planning literature
scope_conditions: general planning and reasoning tasks, position paper accepted at ICML 2024
quoted_support: We argue that auto-regressive LLMs cannot, by themselves, do planning or self-verification (which is after all a form of reasoning)... We present a vision of LLM-Modulo Frameworks that combine the strengths of LLMs with external model-based verifiers in a tighter bi-directional interaction regime.

claim: The paper explicitly rejects both extremes -- LLMs as reliable self-verifying planners, and LLMs as mere syntactic translators for symbolic solvers -- positioning LLMs as valuable generators whose outputs must be checked by external verifiers to be trustworthy.
stance_target: correct framing of the LLM role in search/planning systems that combine generation with verification
scope_conditions: general position paper on LLM planning/reasoning
quoted_support: In this position paper, we take the view that both these extremes are misguided.
